key_idea: A word of length L has L-1 moves and at most L-2 direction changes, so k is effectively bounded by 98 and a DP over (cell, last direction, kinks used) per letter is tiny.
sketch: If k>L-2 answer No (and for L=1 answer Yes iff k=0 and the letter exists). Initialize states for every first move from a cell matching w[0] to a neighbour matching w[1] with 0 kinks. For each next letter extend each reachable (cell, dir, q) in all 8 directions, adding one kink when the direction differs (a reversal counts too), keeping q<=k. Answer Yes iff any state with exactly k kinks survives after the last letter. About 100*100*8*100*8 = 6.4e7 boolean steps. Pitfalls: exactly k, not at most k; letters are space-separated in the input.
